gappers.catalyst: Fourth session of the post-earnings collapse: Q3 revenue +571% and a beat, but FY26 guidance top end cut, data-centre capacity delays flagged and capex raised toward ~$45B; Baird $340->$200, BofA ->$265
gappers.catalyst_detail: Q3 (Nov 12) delivered revenue of $980.8M, +571% YoY and ahead of consensus, with adjusted net income turning positive at +$90.9M from a -$100.4M adjusted loss a year earlier. The market traded the guidance instead: Nebius lowered the top end of FY26 revenue guidance and now expects the low end, attributed data-centre capacity delays, and raised capex toward ~$45B. Shares fell 20.25% on Nov 12 and a further 9.92% on Nov 13, with Baird cutting $340 -> $200 and BofA to $265. Today extends the slide a fourth session, to roughly 64% below the $299.86 52-week high.
gappers.why: Beat the quarter, broke the story. Revenue growth was never the swing factor; a guidance cut plus capacity delays plus a ~$45B capex number converts the thesis from self-funding compounder to capital-hungry builder with execution risk - and it landed into Jensen Huang's resignation as NVIDIA CEO, which de-rated every Nvidia-backed neocloud at once.
gappers.impact: The most damaged chart in the scan and a sustained de-rating, not a one-day spike: -28.8% vs 20-SMA, -44.7% vs 50-SMA, -40.0% vs 200-SMA, and -30.5% across four sessions (154.90 -> 128.91 -> 115.85 -> 107.60) on prior-session volume of 48.9M. Read-through is identical to CRWV - one trade expressed twice, not two signals.
gappers.horizon_reasoning: The guidance reset is structural but structurally BEARISH; a long thesis needs the capex and capacity-delay questions answered first, and XLK fails sector momentum on both 1mo (-10.0%) and 3mo (-10.5%).
gappers.opportunity_cost: ATR(14) is 15.82% of price - the widest in the list - so the mandated 10% stop sits at 0.63 ATR, under two-thirds of an average day, and would fire on noise alone; +20% is only 1.26 ATR. Fails the 2:1 gate outright at every permitted stop distance. Taking it would spend a weekly trade slot on the worst-trending name in the worst-performing sector, one day before the NVDA print that caused the move. Research only, no order.

gappers.catalyst: Sixth session of the neocloud de-rate: a Q3 beat and raised FY26 guide given back in full as Huang's NVIDIA exit repriced Nvidia-backed AI clouds; now ~64% off its 52-week high
gappers.catalyst_detail: Q3 (Nov 10) was a beat, not a miss - revenue $3.66B (up more than $1B sequentially), backlog ~$132.5B (+138% YoY), FY26 guidance raised to $13.0-13.3B against ~$12.9B consensus, and customer concentration improved to no customer above ~35% from ~85% at the start of the year. The stock surged ~25% on the print, then reversed completely over five sessions (60.80 -> 56.59 -> 53.11 -> 53.13 -> 49.68). Source conflict logged and NOT resolved: one feed reports backlog $55.6B (+271% YoY) against three reporting ~$132.5B (+138%); the majority figure is used.
gappers.why: A financing-and-sentiment re-rate, not an earnings problem. The same quarter carried Q3 capex $14.5B, an FY capex guide of $37-39B, $846M of quarterly interest expense and a $709M loss - the equity is a leveraged bet on AI capex continuing. Huang's exit removes the perceived Nvidia backstop for exactly that vendor-financed model, so the market reprices the structure regardless of the backlog beat.
gappers.impact: Sustained repricing rather than a headline spike - six consecutive down sessions on prior-session volume of 80.2M, now ~64% below the $138.25 52-week high, -9.7% vs 20-SMA, -31.6% vs 50-SMA and -44.2% vs 200-SMA. Sector read-through IS the story: NBIS is the identical trade, and BE/BW are its power-derivative expression.
gappers.horizon_reasoning: The driver is a live binary - Huang succession plus NVDA reporting Tuesday after the close at ~±7-9% implied - not a settled reset, and XLK is the worst sector on 1mo and 3mo.
gappers.opportunity_cost: The 10% stop is 0.82 ATR, inside one average day, so it gets taken out by noise before any thesis can resolve; +20% is 1.64 ATR. Cannot clear 2:1 at any permitted stop. It would also spend a weekly slot carrying the NVDA print as an uncompensated overnight binary. The 2026-11-13 log already deferred CRWV until after that print and the 07:09 run reaffirmed it: earliest legitimate look is Wednesday, and nothing today changes that. Research only, no order.

gappers.catalyst: NEW to the scan. No company news today - a pre-earnings de-rate into fiscal Q4 results due Wed Nov 18, giving back a year in which the stock ran +93.6%; fourth straight down session
gappers.catalyst_detail: No KLIC-specific release dated today. Kulicke & Soffa - which supplies the thermocompression and advanced-packaging bonders used in HBM and AI accelerator assembly - reports fiscal Q4 2026 on Wednesday Nov 18. The last reported quarter (fiscal Q3, ended Jul 2026) was exceptional: revenue $330.4M (+122.6% YoY), gross margin 47.8%, operating profit $68.3M (+1,220%), net income $57.4M (+1,845.7%) or $1.07 GAAP / $1.20 non-GAAP per share. Consensus for Wednesday is roughly $1.43-1.46 EPS on ~$384M revenue. Against fiscal-year revenue of $654M (2025), $706M (2024) and $742M (2023), FY2026 is a violent reacceleration. The stock is nonetheless sliding into the print: $72.42 (Nov 11) -> $69.07 (Nov 13) -> gapping $65.00, having been up 93.6% over a year.
gappers.why: Pre-earnings positioning inside a sector-wide de-rate, not a company event. KLIC is advanced-packaging capex beta, so it trades on the same AI-capex doubt as the neoclouds and the power names, and the Nov 18 print is the second binary of its week after NVDA's on Tuesday. Holders who rode +93.6% are de-risking ahead of a number that has to clear a very high bar, and AMKR at rank 7 is the same packaging trade already punished for exactly that.
gappers.impact: Reads as a sustained de-rate, not a spike to fade: four consecutive down sessions, -11.3% vs 20-SMA, -20.8% vs 50-SMA and -25.3% vs 200-SMA. Sector read-through is explicit and confirmatory - AMKR gapped -5.15% on the same driver, and AMKR already reported a Q3 miss with a soft Q4 guide, which is a live preview of the risk in KLIC's Wednesday print. Liquidity is adequate: prior-session consolidated volume 698k shares (~$45M notional), so a $10-20k clip is immaterial, though the IEX-only 20d average of 36k shares understates the real book and a limit order is still required.
gappers.horizon_reasoning: The underlying advanced-packaging growth is genuinely structural, but with earnings two days out the tradeable horizon is dominated by a binary event, not by the thesis - and the thesis cannot be underwritten until Wednesday's number and guide are known.
gappers.opportunity_cost: This is the one row with a real argument rather than a flat rejection, and it is the best ATR fit in the scan: at 6.50% of price the 10% stop is 1.54 ATR and the +20% target 3.08 ATR - the only row where the stop sits outside one average day's range, and the closest any gapper has come to the mid-vol passing band the 2026-11-16 pre-market entry identified. It still fails, on four independent counts: price is 25.3% BELOW its 200-SMA, so the long-bias filter fails outright; price is below the 20-SMA while XLK is the worst sector on 1mo and 3mo, so Rule 9 fails; fiscal Q4 earnings land Wednesday Nov 18, an uncompensated binary two days out, immediately after NVDA's Tuesday print; and a down-gap with no company-specific news is bottom-fishing, which the rulebook forbids without a documented catalyst. Within today's list it dominates BMNR, NBIS, CRWV, BE, BW, AMKR and ONDS on R:R shape, so if any gapper is ever worth a slot it is this one - but the correct action is to spend no slot today and re-examine after Wednesday's print, with a reclaim of the 20-SMA (~$73) as the minimum technical precondition. Research only, no order.

gappers.catalyst: Fourth session giving back a +13% post-earnings spike as AI-power beta: Q3 revenue $1.24B (+138% YoY), guide raised to $4.4-4.6B and a 900MW NTT DATA deal, all outweighed by the AI-capex de-rate
gappers.catalyst_detail: Bloom Energy's Q3 2026 was the strongest fundamental print in this scan: revenue $1.24B (+138% YoY), product revenue up 179%, adjusted operating margin expanding from 8.9% to 23.1%, and FY26 guidance raised again to $4.4-4.6B (~122% growth). It also announced a partnership with NTT DATA to deploy 900MW of fuel-cell power across global data centres, against a delivery record that includes powering an Oracle data centre in 55 days versus a 90-day target. The stock closed $209.47 (+13.0%) on Nov 11 and has fallen every session since - 209.36, 201.94, 191.92, now gapping $181.50, about -13.3% - with no company-specific bad news at any point.
gappers.why: Bloom is an AI-datacentre power derivative, so it trades as AI-capex beta rather than on its own order book. Huang's resignation and the neocloud de-rate dragged the whole AI-power complex down with the chips and the clouds, which is why a company that raised guidance and signed 900MW is down double digits in four sessions. BW at rank 6 is the same trade in a lower-quality wrapper, which confirms the driver is sectoral.
gappers.impact: Mixed, and the most genuinely interesting fundamental story here. The order book and margin trajectory are the best in the scan and the NTT deal is structural, so the drawdown is sector-driven rather than thesis-driven. But the technical read-through is the disqualifier: -11.6% vs 20-SMA, -25.6% vs 50-SMA and -18.8% vs 200-SMA, so the long-bias filter and sector-momentum rule both fail, and it is the same trade as CRWV, NBIS, BW and as TLN/CEG in today's pre-market log.
gappers.horizon_reasoning: Alone among the five the catalyst is structural and intact - 138% revenue growth, a raised guide and 900MW contracted - so the business merits a multi-week swing thesis. The entry is wrong today, not the thesis.
gappers.opportunity_cost: The 10% stop is 0.90 ATR and the +20% target 1.79 ATR, so it fails 2:1 before anything else is considered. More decisively, BE is strictly dominated for the SAME AI-power exposure by TLN from today's pre-market log, whose ATR is 5.13% of price, whose 10% stop is 1.95 ATR and +20% target 3.9 ATR, whose R:R gate actually passes, and which sits above its 20-, 50- and 200-SMA rather than below all three. Both carry the NVDA Tuesday binary, so the right move is to spend no weekly slot on either today and revisit TLN - not BE - after the Nov 18 FOMC minutes. On R:R shape BE is also dominated within today's list by KLIC. BE earns a watchlist slot, not a trade. Research only, no order.
